name: C3
recipe: N/A — c3c is a C/C++ compiler that links libLLVM (versions 19-23) as its codegen backend plus libcurl, configured via CMake. It is NOT a self-contained amalgam (Lane B fails: it pulls the entire LLVM library tree, not a vendorable single-TU source) and has no prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm of itself (Lane A fails). Not Rust/Python/JS (C/D fail). The only near-live angle is C3-to-wasm OUTPUT, which still requires running the libLLVM-backed compiler somewhere first — and our LLVM is shipped as a toolchain, not as a libLLVM the c3c frontend can statically link inside the sandbox without a configure+build chain. To wire it would mean building c3c against our in-sandbox LLVM (C11+C++17 compile of the c3c tree linking libLLVM), an hours-long native-toolchain provisioning task, not a command-recipe.
smoke: N/A — cannot construct a runnable in-sandbox smoke. If c3c were built: echo 'fn int main(){return 0;}' > t.c3 && c3c compile-run --target wasm32 t.c3 — but the compiler binary itself is not producible as plain wasm32-wasi.
blocker: c3c links libLLVM (LLVM 19-23) as a library for codegen plus libcurl for network; needs a CMake configure + C11/C++17 build linking the multi-million-LOC LLVM library tree. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi build of c3c exists, and it is not a self-contained amalgam. Our LLVM is shipped as a toolchain, not as a statically-linkable libLLVM for the c3c frontend. The asked question (run the COMPILER in-sandbox) is gated on a native-toolchain library link + configure chain, not a wiring task. (Note: C3-to-wasm OUTPUT artifacts are a separate, near-live concern but require running this compiler first.)

name: Smalltalk
recipe: No plain wasm32-wasi Smalltalk VM exists. The only WASM path (OpenSmalltalk "Catalyst") is a SqueakJS+WASM browser hybrid that REQUIRES a JS coordination layer (synchronized JS<->WASM object memory) — not a standalone .wasm, so Lane A/B are out. The C OpenSmalltalk VM is Slang/Cog-generated with image-snapshot mmap + GC + heavy platform glue (not a clean amalgam) — Lane B impractical. Viable lane = D (JS): run SqueakJS, a pure-JS Squeak/OpenSmalltalk image interpreter, on QuickJS/esbuild. Headless entrypoint is squeak_node.js. Bundle vm.*.js modules + vm.plugins.*.js, disable the optional jit.js, and ship a Squeak .image file as a data input. UI plugins (canvas/DOM/events) must be stubbed; only headless/compute execution is in scope.
smoke: In the JS lane, load SqueakJS headless + a minimal Squeak .image and evaluate `3 + 4` via the bytecode interpreter, asserting it returns 7 (and `(1 to: 10) inject: 0 into: [:a :b | a + b]` => 55) to stdout — no canvas/DOM, no JIT.
blocker: SqueakJS headless targets Node.js (squeak_node.js) and assumes Node globals/fs + browser-ish APIs; bare QuickJS/esbuild fidelity is unverified, and it requires shipping a multi-MB Squeak .image file plus stubbing all UI plugins. Not a wasm32-wasi VM at all. (Catalyst's WASM is JS-coupled -> impossible as standalone; OpenSmalltalk C VM is generated/snapshot-based -> not a Lane-B amalgam.)

name: Modula-2
recipe: No prebuilt wasm exists (Lane A=no; gm2 is a GCC front-end, GCC->wasm impractical). Only path is Lane B via the classic m2c translator (Sinuhe's fork of m2c-0.6 by Vladimir Makarov, GPLv2, git.savannah.nongnu.org/srv/git/m2c.git; mirrors at github.com/m2sf/m2c and github.com/GunterMueller/Modula-2_to_C_Transpilers). m2c is C-hosted, emits C99/K&R C, ships a C runtime lib, supports PIM3/PIM4 + an "improved coroutine module." Build it OFFLINE on a provisioned host first: it's autotools (configure) + yacc/lex, so pre-generate the parser/lexer .c and the config header, then feed ONLY the resulting .c + runtime to our C lane (:include_only/:compile_only on the amalgam) — never run configure/yacc in-sandbox. The translator binary itself (m2c.wasm) plausibly compiles. The HARD part is the emitted program's runtime: SYSTEM.NEWPROCESS/TRANSFER (Modula-2's defining coroutine/concurrency primitives) require allocating a fresh stack and switching SP, classically via ucontext makecontext/setcontext or inline asm. wasm32-wasi has NO ucontext, NO stack-switching, and C cannot set the WASM stack pointer (protected call stack); the WASM stack-switching proposal is not in stable wasmtime. So programs using coroutines CANNOT run. Only the sequential subset (no PROCESS/TRANSFER, ISO/PIM straight-line + std modules) would translate and run. Reject MOCKA (x86-asm backend only, no C), MOTTO ("repurposed Apr 2023, rework will take time", incomplete), m2sf/m2c (M2R10 BSK subset only, no PIM/ISO, no coroutines).
smoke: Sequential-only smoke (the only thing that can pass): translate a Hello.mod (IMPORT InOut/STextIO; WriteString; no PROCESS) with the m2c translator, then C-lane-compile the emitted .c + m2c runtime to wasm32-wasi, run under wasmtime, assert stdout "Hello, Modula-2". The DEFINITIVE blocker test: any program using SYSTEM.NEWPROCESS + TRANSFER (e.g. a two-coroutine producer/consumer) — emitted C will reference ucontext/stack-switch and fail to compile or trap at link/run, confirming concurrency is unsupported.
blocker: Modula-2's core feature — SYSTEM coroutines (NEWPROCESS/TRANSFER, the concurrency the brief flags) — needs native stack allocation + SP switching (ucontext/asm) that wasm32-wasi cannot provide (no ucontext, opaque/protected WASM call stack, stack-switching proposal not in stable wasmtime). The full language is effectively impossible in-sandbox; only the sequential subset (no PROCESS) is live-likely, and even that requires offline-pre-generated yacc/lex+configure artifacts for the m2c translator before it can enter our C lane (no in-sandbox configure/codegen).

name: Pkl
recipe: No viable lane. Pkl is a JVM/Truffle (GraalVM) language. Distribution is either (a) JVM jar requiring HotSpot JIT, or (b) GraalVM native-image binaries (native ELF/Mach-O, not wasm). The only Pkl-to-wasm path is GraalVM Web Image (--tool:svm-wasm), which is experimental and emits a wasm MODULE PAIRED WITH A JS LAUNCHER/runtime that targets a browser or Node.js JS host — not a plain wasm32-wasi module loadable by wasmtime. This is precisely the excluded js-pair form for Lane A. There is no bare wasm32-wasi Pkl build; not C/C++ (Lane B), not a Rust crate (Lane C), not pure-Python/JS-on-QuickJS (Lane D). The Pkl codebase is Java/Kotlin on Truffle (megabytes of bytecode + GraalVM polyglot internals), not portable through mrustc or our C/C++ amalgam lane.
smoke: N/A — no artifact to run under wasmtime. (Hypothetically, the only thing produced would be `pkl.js` + `pkl.js.wasm` requiring a JS engine; loading `pkl.js.wasm` standalone under `wasmtime run pkl.js.wasm` fails — it has JS-runtime imports, not WASI, and no CLI entrypoint.)
blocker: JVM/Truffle language: requires HotSpot JIT or a GraalVM native binary. Only wasm route is GraalVM Web Image, which is a browser/Node JS-coupled wasm+JS pair (experimental, JS-host imports), not a standalone wasm32-wasi module for wasmtime. Excluded by the js-pair / JIT criteria.

name: Yorick
recipe: Lane B (self-contained C), but NOT drop-in — needs a port. The core interpreter (yorick/*.c: parse.c, ops*.c, array.c, ydata.c, yorick.c) is portable ANSI C and compiles to wasm32-wasi routinely. BLOCKERS to resolve before :compile_only works: (1) Yorick's `configure`/`play/unix/config.sh` detects features by COMPILING AND RUNNING probe binaries (./fputest, ./cfg) — impossible under wasi at config time, so we must HAND-AUTHOR a static config.h/Make.cfg for the wasm target (no autodetect). (2) The interp sits entirely on the `play` portability layer for I/O AND the event loop, not just graphics. Build with NO_XLIB=yes (drops gist/X11/OpenGL) and supply a minimal wasi `play/unix` backend: keep timeu/timew/dir/yio paths; STUB OUT uspawn.c (fork/exec), usock.c (sockets), udl.c (dlopen plugins), and SIGFPE delivery in handler.c; replace the poll/select event loop (uevent.c/upoll.c) with a non-interactive batch driver that feeds a .i script and runs to completion. Compile: clang.wasm core/*.c + play/std + stubbed play/unix with a pregenerated config.h, define USE_SELECT off, no plugins. Estimate: real porting work (hand-written wasi play backend + config.h), thousands of LOC touched, not an amalgam drop-in.
smoke: echo 'x = span(0,1,5); write, format="%g\n", x(sum);' > t.i && yorick -batch t.i  # expect 2.5 (sum of 0,.25,.5,.75,1)
blocker: Two non-trivial gates: (1) configure detects features by running compiled probe binaries — cross-compile to wasm needs a hand-authored static config.h (no autodetect possible under wasi). (2) The portable-C core is wired into the POSIX `play` layer for the event loop + I/O; fork (uspawn), sockets (usock), dlopen plugins (udl), and SIGFPE handling must be stubbed and the poll/select interactive loop replaced with a batch driver. Portable C means it CAN be ported, but it's a bespoke wasi-backend porting effort, not a self-contained amalgam drop-in. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi exists.

name: Gatsby
recipe: N/A — Gatsby is a Node-runtime build orchestrator, not a portable wasm-able library. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (not Lane A). Not C/C++ (not B). Not a Rust crate (not C). It is JS but cannot run on QuickJS/esbuild as a self-contained module (not D): the `gatsby build` pipeline hard-requires the full Node runtime + a native lmdb-store addon (LMDB cache), webpack bundling, a Redux/LMDB-backed GraphQL data layer, and parallel query running via OS worker pools (n-1 Node cluster/child_process workers). These depend on native node-gyp addons, multi-process fork/exec, threads, and pervasive fs/process APIs unavailable to a single-threaded wasm32-wasi instance under wasmtime.
smoke: n/a — cannot construct a smoke test; `gatsby build` cannot initialize without Node + native LMDB addon + worker fork/exec under wasmtime.
blocker: Requires full Node runtime: native lmdb-store node-gyp addon (LMDB cache), webpack, GraphQL data layer, and parallel query running via OS worker pools (Node cluster/child_process fork-exec, threads). Fork-exec + native addons + threads are unavailable to single-threaded wasm32-wasi under wasmtime.

name: Vike
recipe: No viable lane. Vike is a Vite plugin (formerly vite-plugin-ssr): pure JS itself, but its whole purpose is orchestrating Vite's Node-runtime build/dev chain (esbuild native binary + Rollup) plus a JS server (Express/Hono/etc.). Lane D (QuickJS/esbuild) cannot host Vike because Vike does not bundle/compile by itself — it drives Vite, which depends on the esbuild native binary and a full Node runtime (fs/net/server middleware, dev-server with HMR/network). esbuild itself is a Go native binary (no plain wasm32-wasi build under wasmtime; its wasm path is browser/Node-WASI-emscripten-shaped and needs a JS host). The dev server is network-purposed (browser+HMR) = impossible. The SSG output step alone is doable in principle but only as the tail of a full Vite build that we cannot stand up in-sandbox. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm (A), not C/C++ (B), not a Rust crate (C).
smoke: N/A — no lane. If a Vite-in-sandbox stack existed: `vike build` on a minimal page then check dist/client/index.html renders SSG markup. Cannot run: Vike has no standalone CLI that bypasses Vite; it requires the esbuild native toolchain + Node server runtime, neither available as plain wasm32-wasi under wasmtime.
blocker: Vike is inseparable from Vite's Node-runtime build chain: esbuild (Go native binary, no plain wasm32-wasi build) + Rollup + a JS server, and a network/browser dev server with HMR. No standalone path; depends on native exec and network-purposed server. Lane D (QuickJS/esbuild) can't host it because Vike orchestrates Vite rather than compiling anything itself.

name: Wakuwork / Waku
blocker: Waku is a Node.js + Vite React Server Components framework, not a standalone program. There is no prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm (rules out Lane A). It is a JS app dependent on a full Node runtime: Vite/esbuild/Rollup dev+build server, the React server-component bundler, and the RSC Flight wire protocol streamed from a live Node/Vite process. Even the "Pure SSG" slice runs the Node build pipeline (Vite + react-server-dom-webpack/rollup, hundreds of npm deps, native-ish bundler internals) to emit HTML — it is a running Node server doing the prerender, not a pure self-contained build that QuickJS/esbuild-on-wasm could execute. Lane D (JS on QuickJS/esbuild) cannot host Vite's plugin pipeline, Rollup, the RSC flight serializer, or the React server renderer. Not C/C++ (B) or Rust (C). The whole value (RSC server runtime, Flight protocol, Vite HMR) is a Node-server purpose that our in-sandbox wasm32-wasi + QuickJS environment cannot provide.

name: Vite
recipe: None viable. Vite is a Node.js application with no plain wasm32-wasi build. Lane A: no prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists; Vite is distributed as npm Node packages. Lane B: not C/C++. Lane C: not a bare Rust crate (Vite core is TypeScript/Node; its bundler Rolldown is a multi-crate Rust+NAPI native addon, edition2021+, proc-macros, NAPI host bindings — impossible under mrustc). Lane D: not pure-Python, and not runnable on QuickJS/esbuild — it is a long-running Node server depending on the full Node platform.
smoke: N/A — cannot run. Even minimally, `vite --version` requires Node's module system, native esbuild (Go binary), and Rolldown's NAPI native binary; none load under wasm32-wasi/wasmtime.
blocker: Long-running Node dev server: native HTTP listener + websockets (HMR) + fs watch = network-purpose + long-running server. Build path depends on native binaries — esbuild (Go native exec) and Rolldown/Rollup (Rust NAPI native addon). No plain wasm32-wasi artifact; requires full Node platform (fork/exec, sockets, native addons). All disqualifiers (network-purpose, long-running server, fork-exec native binaries) trip impossible.

name: Webpack
recipe: No viable lane. Webpack is a full Node.js application, not a single self-contained JS file. Lane D (QuickJS/esbuild) needs pure-JS that runs without a Node runtime; Webpack depends on Node worker_threads, the full Node fs/module system, enhanced-resolve, watchpack file watching, and a loader pipeline where loaders fork-exec or call native addons (sass-embedded, esbuild-loader, terser/SWC). QuickJS has no Node API surface, no worker_threads, no real module/fs graph. Lanes A/B/C do not apply (no prebuilt wasm32-wasi build, not C/C++, not Rust).
smoke: N/A — no buildable artifact. Conceptual check: webpack ./src/index.js -o dist/ requires Node + worker_threads + loader fork-exec, none available under bare wasmtime.
blocker: Full Node.js program: worker_threads, Node fs/module internals, enhanced-resolve, watchpack, and loaders that fork-exec / load native addons (sass-embedded, esbuild-loader, terser). No pure-JS single-file form runs on QuickJS. fork-exec + native-threads → impossible under bare wasm32-wasi/wasmtime.

name: txiki.js
recipe: No viable lane. txiki.js is architecturally a libuv-based runtime: README states it "uses QuickJS-ng as its JavaScript engine and libuv as the platform layer." libuv provides async I/O, TCP/UDP sockets, native event-loop, child_process (fork-exec), and curl HTTP — all of which require native syscalls / network / process spawning absent under plain wasm32-wasi (jitless wasmtime). Lane A: no prebuilt PLAIN wasm32-wasi artifact (repo's 0.3% WASM is incidental; there is no standalone wasm target, only native + the usual emscripten-ish experiments). Lane B (self-contained C): the C engine compiles, but txiki.js minus libuv is not txiki.js — every web/runtime API (fs, net, timers, signals, process) routes through libuv's native event loop, which cannot be satisfied in-sandbox. Lane C/D: N/A. Crucially, the JS-execution core (QuickJS-ng) is ALREADY LIVE as qjs in-sandbox, so the engine value is covered; the delta txiki.js offers IS the libuv platform layer, which is precisely the impossible part.
smoke: N/A — cannot build a standalone wasm32-wasi tjs.wasm. If one attempted, the smoke would be: `echo 'console.log(1+1)' | tjs run -` expecting "2"; but any test exercising tjs's actual surface (tjs.connect TCP, setTimeout via libuv loop, fs async, fetch via curl) faults on missing native event-loop/socket syscalls. For the JS-eval value alone, use the already-live qjs: `echo 'console.log(1+1)' | qjs -` => 2.
blocker: libuv platform layer: native event loop, sockets/network, fork-exec (child_process), and curl HTTP — none available under jitless wasm32-wasi/wasmtime. The JS engine value (QuickJS-ng) is already covered by the live qjs; the unique delta txiki.js adds is exactly the unsatisfiable native layer.

name: LLRT
recipe: N/A — not portable to wasm32-wasi as a standalone runtime. LLRT is a large Rust (edition 2021, async/Tokio) binary whose value over bare QuickJS is precisely its network surface: built-in AWS SDK clients, llhttp, TLS warmup (LLRT_SDK_CONNECTION_WARMUP), and net allow/deny (LLRT_NET_ALLOW/DENY), all bound to the AWS Lambda Custom Runtime on Amazon Linux 2023. The repo ships no WASM target and explicitly marks WASM-JS-API / WASM-WEB-API as unsupported. Porting would require building Tokio reactor + TLS + AWS SDK + HTTP networking under wasm32-wasi (no sockets/threads), which defeats both the runtime and our sandbox model.
smoke: N/A — would-be smoke (run an AWS SDK / fetch handler) is exactly the network-purpose path that is impossible in-sandbox. The reusable engine core, QuickJS, is already LIVE as `qjs`: e.g. `echo 'print(2+3)' | qjs -` → 5.
blocker: Network-purpose serverless runtime: Tokio async I/O + sockets + TLS + built-in AWS SDK/HTTP networking, AWS-Lambda-bound, no WASM target (repo marks WASM API unsupported). The only sandbox-viable part — the QuickJS JS engine — is already LIVE as `qjs`. LLRT adds nothing runnable in-sandbox.

name: XS (Moddable)
recipe: Build ONLY the standalone `xst` shell, NOT the Moddable SDK (skip mcconfig/xsbug/embedded HALs/GTK simulator entirely). All inputs are checked-in C with no codegen/configure/generated-config.h. Compile against wasm32-wasi (clang.wasm, :compile_only amalgam-style): sources = xs/sources/*.c (xsAll, xsAPI, xsRun, xsMemory, xsLexical, xsSyntaxical, xsScript, xsModule, xsPlatforms.c [the portable shim, NOT lin_xs.c/GLib], + ~50 others), the bundled fdlibm math lib (xs/tools/fdlibm/*.c — e_*, k_*, s_*), bundled yaml (xs/tools/yaml), textdecoder/encoder/base64 modules, and the shell xs/tools/xst.c + xst.h. Defines from xst.mk: -DINCLUDE_XSPLATFORM -DXSPLATFORM=\"xst.h\" -DmxNoConsole=1, and crucially -DmxMultipleThreads=0 (release default uses threads; force single-thread) so no pthread/-latomic/-ldl needed. Includes: xs/includes, xs/platforms, xs/sources, xs/tools, xs/tools/fdlibm, xs/tools/yaml. Skip xst262.c/xstFuzz.c (test262 Agent harness — these are the ONLY pthread+socket+condvar users, reached solely in `-2`/262 mode, irrelevant to plain JS eval). main() runs scripts via fxRunProgramFile / modules via fxRunModuleFile using plain fopen/fread/printf — all WASI-satisfiable. No JIT (XS is a bytecode interpreter), no GPU, no network, no fork/exec in the eval path. Link as wasm32-wasi command module.
smoke: echo 'globalThis.print ? print("hi "+(1+2)) : trace("hi "+(1+2)+"\n");' > /tmp/t.js ; wasmtime --dir=/tmp xst.wasm /tmp/t.js  # expect: hi 3 . Also: echo 'trace((typeof JSON)+" "+JSON.stringify({a:[1,2,3].map(x=>x*x)})+"\n")' > /tmp/u.js ; wasmtime --dir=/tmp xst.wasm /tmp/u.js  # exercises lexer+VM+JSON+arrow+array, expect: object {"a":[1,4,9]}
blocker: Threads/sockets exist in xst262.c/xstFuzz.c (test262 SharedArrayBuffer Agent cluster: pthread_create + condvars) but are excluded by building only xst.c with -DmxMultipleThreads=0; the plain JS-eval path is single-threaded libc-stdio only. Residual risk: a few engine sources may reference atomics (xsAtomics.c) — compile-time wasm atomics are fine without wasi-threads; only runtime thread *spawning* (omitted) would break. Date/time uses time()/gmtime (WASI clock OK). Must hand-write a tiny build (the SDK makefile assumes native gcc + $MODDABLE env), but object list is fully enumerated in xst.mk.

name: Nova
recipe: No viable lane. Lane C (mrustc ~1.74) is the only Rust path and cannot build Nova: workspace is Rust edition 2024, rust-toolchain pinned to 1.92.0, deps are large + proc-macro + SIMD (oxc_parser/oxc_ast/oxc_semantic, sonic-rs, ecmascript_atomics, temporal_rs, soavec, num-bigint, regex, hashbrown). edition2024 + proc-macros = impossible under mrustc. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm (Lane A); not C/C++ (Lane B); not Python/JS-on-QuickJS (Lane D). Engine has no wasm execution. Architecturally no-JIT/no-GPU/no-native-thread so it WOULD cross-compile to wasm32-wasi under a real modern rustc, but the sandbox lacks that toolchain. Live qjs already covers the JS-engine need.
smoke: If built: pipe console.log(40+2) to nova-cli run under wasmtime, expect 42. Not achievable on current lanes.
blocker: Rust edition 2024 + toolchain 1.92.0 + proc-macro/SIMD deps (oxc_*, sonic-rs, ecmascript_atomics) exceed the mrustc ~1.74 Lane-C ceiling; no prebuilt wasm32-wasi artifact and no C/Python/JS lane applies. JS-engine need already met by live qjs.

name: Kiesel
recipe: No viable recipe. Lane A requires a prebuilt PLAIN wasm32-wasi .wasm; Kiesel ships none. Its build.zig defines only UEFI (bootx64) + generic native targets — no wasm32-wasi target is wired. The only WASM build is the in-browser playground (kiesel.dev/playground), a JS-host-paired/browser build, explicitly excluded by Lane A. Core engine defaults to bdwgc (Boehm GC, C) for garbage collection and libregexp; Intl/Temporal pull ICU4X + temporal_rs via cargo/Rust (outside all lanes). All four deps (enable-libgc/libregexp/intl/temporal) are toggleable off, but disabling GC removes garbage collection, making it unusable for real JS. bdwgc does not cleanly target wasm32-wasi (stack-scanning/threads). Self-building to wasm32-wasi would require a wasi-compatible GC swap + dropping Intl/Temporal — speculative. Not a self-contained C/C++ (Lane B), not Rust (C), not Python/JS-on-qjs (D). Already covered: JS execution is LIVE via qjs (QuickJS); Kiesel is young with partial ECMAScript and adds nothing over qjs.
smoke: If a wasm32-wasi build existed: echo 'print(1+2)' | wasmtime kiesel.wasm /dev/stdin and expect 3. (No such artifact exists; the playground is browser-only.) For our actual JS needs, qjs is already LIVE: echo 'console.log(1+2)' | wasmtime qjs.wasm -.
blocker: No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm — build.zig wires only UEFI + native; the sole WASM is a browser/js-pair playground (excluded by Lane A). Core requires bdwgc (Boehm GC, C) which does not target wasm32-wasi cleanly; Intl/Temporal need cargo/Rust. JS already covered LIVE by qjs (QuickJS), making Kiesel redundant.

name: Porffor
recipe: Lane D JS on QuickJS. Bundle ESM compiler to one qjs script, pure JS acorn, shim fs and process, emit wasm to disk only.
smoke: Emit add.wasm under qjs; check magic header and wasmtime validate.
blocker: No prebuilt wasm; needs bundling and fs shims; run mode needs WebAssembly global qjs lacks.

name: Volta
recipe: N/A — out of scope by purpose. Volta is a Node/npm/yarn toolchain version manager: it downloads native toolchain binaries over the network, installs them on the host filesystem, and manages PATH via shim executables it fork-execs. Every one of those operations (network fetch, host-FS install, PATH shimming, fork-exec of native node) is exactly what the wasm32-wasi sandbox forbids. The Rust binary could theoretically cross-compile toward wasip1 (Lane C territory), but the result would be inert — there is no host PATH to shim, no native Node to install/run, no outbound network. The artifact's reason to exist evaporates inside the sandbox.
smoke: N/A — nothing to smoke-test; the tool has no meaningful in-sandbox behavior (no PATH, no native node to install/exec, no network).
blocker: Purpose is host-PATH management + network download + fork-exec of native Node/npm/yarn binaries. None of these exist or are permitted under wasm32-wasi/wasmtime. A compiled .wasm would be a no-op shell. Out of scope.

name: go mod
recipe: None viable. (A) No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi build of the Go `go` command exists — Go ships GOOS=wasip1 as a *target* (compile Go programs TO wasm), not a wasm build of the toolchain ITSELF. (B/C/D) N/A — `go mod` is Go source, not C/Rust-crate/pure-Python/JS. Even cross-compiling cmd/go to wasip1 yields a non-functional `go mod`: the go command is a process orchestrator that fork/execs the compiler, linker, assembler, and VCS tools, and `os/exec` is stubbed to ENOSYS on wasip1 (no proc_exec/fork in WASI preview1). `go mod download`/`tidy` additionally need network to proxy.golang.org, which the no-network sandbox forbids. Offline modes (GOPROXY=off, -mod=vendor, -mod=readonly) only avoid network for an ALREADY-populated cache/vendor dir — they don't make the orchestrator runnable without exec. We already run Go via yaegi (interpreter), which does not use the go toolchain or modules.
smoke: N/A — cannot construct a runnable artifact. If one tried: `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm` build of cmd/go, then `wasmtime go.wasm mod tidy` would fail at first subprocess spawn (os/exec ENOSYS on wasip1) and, for un-cached deps, at network dial — neither available in-sandbox.
blocker: fork/exec: the `go` command orchestrates subprocess tools (compile/link/asm/vcs) via os/exec, which is ENOSYS on wasip1 (WASI preview1 has no proc_exec/fork). Secondary blocker: module fetch needs network to proxy.golang.org, forbidden in the no-network sandbox. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi build of the toolchain exists either.

name: dep

name: cpanm
recipe: No viable lane. cpanm is a pure-Perl script but (1) requires a Perl interpreter that is NOT live in-sandbox — perl is absent from the live list, and "webperl" is an Emscripten/browser build, not a plain wasm32-wasi binary for wasmtime (excludes lane A by the no-emscripten/js-pair rule); (2) its core function is fork/exec orchestration — it spawns tar, make, perl Makefile.PL, and Build.PL subprocesses per distribution to configure/build/test, which WASI cannot do; (3) it is a network-purpose tool, fetching dist metadata and tarballs from cpanmetadb.plackperl.org and metacpan.org over HTTPS. Lanes B/C/D do not apply (not C/C++, not Rust, not Python/JS).
